concepts.def: Burning fossil fuels, deforestation and intensive farming increase greenhouse gas emissions, pollute air and water, and degrade ecosystems.
Rising global temperatures bring sea-level rise, more extreme weather and shifting habitats, affecting people unevenly across the world.
The total greenhouse gas emissions caused by a person, product or organisation, usually expressed in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent.
Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
Energy from naturally replenished sources such as wind, solar and hydro power, which produce little or no carbon emissions in use.
The waste hierarchy: cutting consumption first, then reusing items, then recycling materials, to reduce landfill and resource use.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Managing Our Environment — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Managing Our Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Managing Our Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs
Maximising economic growth at any cost
Banning all use of natural resources
Building only in existing cities

mcqs.q: Which gas contributes most to the enhanced greenhouse effect from human activity?
options: Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Hydrogen

mcqs.q: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
options: Wind
Coal
Natural gas
Oil

mcqs.q: In the waste hierarchy, the most preferred option is to:
options: Reduce consumption
Recycle materials
Send waste to landfill
Incinerate waste

mcqs.q: Is the greenhouse effect itself a bad thing?
options: Sustainable describes a building that cannot fall down.
All greenhouse warming is harmful and unnatural.
The greenhouse effect is caused by glass buildings reflecting sunlight.
No — the natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough to be habitable; the problem is the enhanced effect caused by extra emissions from human activity.

mcqs.q: Is recycling the most effective way to manage waste?
options: Recycling means burning waste to generate electricity.
Sustainable describes a building that cannot fall down.
It helps, but reducing consumption and reusing items save more energy and resources; recycling still uses energy for collection and reprocessing.
As long as waste is recycled, how much we consume doesn't matter.
Recycling means burning waste to generate electricity.
Sustainable describes a building that cannot fall down.
Sustainability is purely about protecting nature.
Not only — sustainability balances environmental protection with social fairness and economic viability, so a scheme must also work for people and economies long term.
